previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of coronary artery disease, systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic foot ulcers from prior frostbite, was admitted for worsening left foot pain, swelling, and erythema despite two weeks of oral antibiotics. Imaging revealed osteomyelitis in the fourth and fifth toes, and he was admitted for IV antibiotic therapy and source control. He underwent podiatric debridement of the affected toes, and a PICC line was placed to complete a 14-day course of IV vancomycin and ciprofloxacin. His pain was managed with scheduled and breakthrough opioids, with plans to taper upon improvement. His cardiac medications were held initially due to hypotension but were restarted before discharge. He was transitioned to extended care for antibiotic completion and was discharged in stable condition with follow-up arranged in podiatry, cardiology, and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
 ___ is a ___ with PMH of CAD s/p multiple PCI, sCHF (EF 
___, Atrial fibrillation on rivaroxaban and hepatitis 
C who presents to ED with L toe pain and dyspnea in the setting 
of medication noncompliance (torsemide), believed to have a CHF 
and COPD exacerbation. He was diuresed with 60 mg IV lasix ___ 
times daily, and was net negative approximately 2L. Due to poor 
movement of air, diffuse expiratory wheezing, and cough 
productive of sputum, we treated him for a COPD exacerbation 
with a five day course of levofloxacin and prednisone 
(___). Podiatry evaluated the patient during this 
admission and felt that the patient was at baseline, without 
active infection, and recommended follow up in their clinic.

His hospital stay was notable for syncopal event without loss of 
consciousness, that occured in the setting of straining for a 
bowel movement. CT was negative. EKG showed a. fib without RVR. 
Electrolytes WNL, serum tox negative, urine tox negative. It was 
felt to be a vagal event. He had no further events during his 
hospitalization.

# L Foot pain: Xray in ED without evidence for acute bone 
destruction. Podiatry evaluated in ED and reported no signs of 
osteo or deeper infection appreciated. Per podiatry 
recommendations, no antibiotics necessary at this time. We 
controlled his pain with oxycodone prn.  
 
# sCHF (EF ___: Most consistent with acute 
exacerbation in the setting of medication noncompliance due to 
access to obtaining home meds. Reports some weight gain, 
orthopnea and dyspnea on exertion and his JVP is elevated though 
no ___ which he has experienced previously.  pBNP elevated to 
6854. We restarted torsemide 20 mg daily and continued his home 
carvedilol and lisinopril. We diuresed him with IV lasix for a 
net negative of ___ L this admission. 

#COPD: CXR PA/Lat in ED read as possible new opacities 
concerning for pneumonia. However, his CXR looks largely 
unchanged from prior with evidence of pulmonary edema in the 
setting of systolic CHF exacerbation. WBC 6 on admission. 
However, his WBC increased to WBC of 14. Given his elevated WBC, 
dyspnea, diffuse wheezing on exam, we felt he was having a COPD 
exacerbation.  We treated with levofloxacin and prednison with a 
planned five day course ___. Upon initiating this 
treatment, his dyspnea improved significantly and he was 
breathing comfortably on the day of discharge.    

# Syncopal event: syncopal event occured on ___ without loss 
of consciousness, in the setting of straining for a bowel 
movement. With a question of possible head strike, we obtained a 
CT which was negative. EKG showed a. fib without RVR. 
Electrolytes WNL, serum tox negative, urine tox negative. It was 
felt to be a vagal event. He had no further events during his 
hospitalization.

# Homelessness: Patient reportedly did not take his torsemide 
because he was unable to have it filled. I am concerned that his 
acess to medications is the primary factor resulting in his 
readmission. Social work saw him this admission.  Prior to 
discharge, we filled an entire month of his medications. He had 
a place to stay with the help of his sister.
